summary: Hsu Yun was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Changkai (~1858–1859), Miaolian (~1859), and Yaocheng. He founded the Buddhist Association of China in 1953, where he served as honorary chairman.

Hsu-feng Lee is a Buddhist studies scholar. Lee completed a master's degree at Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies under Huimin and a PhD at the University of Sydney under Mark Allon (attested 2017).

Hsuan Hua was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Chang Chih/Chang Zhi (~1936–1946) and Hsu Yun (1948). He served as Abbot of Tathagata Monastery (~1976–1995) and founded the Buddhist Text Translation Society in 1970.
Hsueh-li Cheng works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Cheng held posts at Ohio University and at the University of Hawaiʻi at Hilo (~1976–2012).

Hu Shih worked in philosophy, sinology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Cornell, Columbia (PhD 1915–1917), and Teachers College under John Dewey and Kaiten Nukariya, he served as Peking University chancellor (1946–1948) and Academia Sinica president (1957–1962).

Huabei Tan is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Tan pursued an English-medium PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under supervisor Medawachchiye Dhammajothi (attested 2026).

Huai-Chin Nan worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. He studied at the ROC Military Academy and University of Nanking, and under Huanxian Yuan. His posts included the ROC Military Academy, Chinese Culture University (~1963–1975), National Chengchi University, and Fu Jen Catholic University.

Huaiyu Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. Chen earned a master's at Peking University under Xinjiang Rong (1994), completed a doctorate under Stephen F. Teiser, and became assistant professor at Arizona State University (~2008).

Huanhuan He works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Posts include Zhejiang University (professor, attested 2015), University of Tokyo (attested 2015), Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (research fellow, attested 2026).

Hubert Decleer was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Koninklijk Atheneum Oostende, Hoger Technisch Instituut Oostende, and KU Leuven under Étienne Lamotte (1975). He held posts including academic director (1987) and senior faculty advisor (1999) at SIT Graduate Institute.

Hubert Durt specialized in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology, studying under Étienne Lamotte (~1959–1968). He held posts at EFEO (~1970–2001), Hōbōgirin Institute (~1978–2004), and International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996–2011).

Hugh B. Urban is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1992–1998) studying under Wendy Doniger, Bruce Lincoln, and Tony K. Stewart, and was appointed associate professor at Ohio State University (~1998).

Hugh Edward Richardson was a Tibetologist who studied at Keble College, Oxford (~1924–1928). He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1930–1950) and was named an Honorary Fellow of the British Academy (1952) and Keble College, Oxford (1981).

Hugh Gray was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Battersea Grammar School, he held posts at SOAS University of London and the University of London as a lecturer (~1960–1981).

Hugh J. Silverman was a philosopher who completed a doctorate at Stanford (~1969–1973). He was a professor at Stony Brook University (1974) and held posts at Stanford (~1972–1974), University of Vienna (2000–2001), and Academy of Fine Arts Vienna (2009–2010).

Hugo David is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He earned a PhD from École Pratique des Hautes Études (-2012) and studied under multiple traditional teachers. He held a fellowship at Cambridge (2013–2014) and became a permanent member of EFEO (2015).
Hugo Enomiya-Lassalle was a scholar in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied under Kyozo Yamada (~1968–1989) and held a post at Sophia University (~1935).
Huidi Zeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Yi-hsun Huang (attested 2011).
Huifeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2007) and held a post at the University of Hong Kong.

Huimin is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1986–1992). He held posts at National Taiwan University of Arts (~1992), Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1992–2007), and was president of Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts (~2014–2022).
